_comment: Single source of truth for how every consumer discovers the ADR corpus. Five sites used to glob it five different ways and had already drifted apart (check_adr_status.py saw 565 files, AdrStorage saw 709). JSON rather than YAML because Python reads it with stdlib json and Kotlin with kotlinx-serialization, both with zero added dependencies. See #520.
_comment_classes: Three distinct classes, not one. An ADR is a dated decision record under `root`. An archived ADR keeps its dated name but leaves the live corpus. A file under `deferred/` is backlog, NOT a decision: it carries slug names, no real date, and statuses from a different vocabulary. Treating it as a decision is what produced 129 files the gate could not see.

backlogVocabulary._comment: A separate vocabulary, deliberately. A backlog entry asks 'is this still worth doing', a decision asks 'is this still the answer we chose'. The two lifecycles are different, so forcing one onto the other destroys meaning: mapping the 35 open backlog entries onto `open` would then age them against the 30-day rule, and they are dated 2000-01-01 because they were never dated at all. See #516.

reviewBy._comment: The 30-day staleness rule was a number nobody chose: no ADR ever said 'we will revisit this in 30 days', so the rule was really 'someone picked a default and wrote it into a gate'. An explicit `review-by:` frontmatter field replaces it for any decision that has one, and 30 days stays only as the fallback for the ones that do not (#527). Grounded in the R criterion of 'A Definition of Done for Architectural Decision Making' — a decision is not done until you have said when you will revisit it. Optional, not required: 0 of 566 decisions carried it when this landed, and making it required would redden the build on debt the rule itself created.

immutableSince._comment: A closed decision's body is a record of what was decided; changing it is a rewrite of history, and the way to say something new is a superseding ADR (#528). This is the date the rule starts applying. It is a floor, not an exemption: 95 of 556 closed decisions had their bodies rewritten before this date, several in the bulk frontmatter migration of 2026-10-07..10. Flagging that history on day one would redden the build on debt that predates the rule — and a gate that fires on 95 known cases gets re-run with a flag and then ignored. Anything closed AFTER this date is policed.

_comment_links.supersedes: frontmatter key on the NEWER ADR naming the one it replaces
_comment_links.superseded-by: frontmatter key on the OLDER ADR naming its replacement; required when status is superseded

frontmatter._comment: The frontmatter contract, declared once. Three code paths used to own it separately — AdrStorage.writeAdr, normalize-adr-frontmatter.py's KNOWN_KEYS, and resolve_stale_adr_status.py's regex surgery — and they had already drifted: updateAdr started writing `review-by` in #527 and the normalizer rejected its own tool's output as 'unknown frontmatter key' (proven, 2026-10-11). Python reads this with stdlib json, Kotlin with kotlinx-serialization. See #518.
frontmatter._comment_knownKeys: An allowlist, not a passthrough, and the reason is specific: a body written INSIDE the frontmatter block still parses as valid YAML, so nothing else catches it. Emitting those 'keys' is how a body gets duplicated into the file. An unknown key is therefore a hard error in the normalizer, which means every key a writer emits MUST appear here or the corpus breaks itself. `gh`, `issue`, `backlog` and `tracked-as` were added on 2026-10-11 after 11 real ADRs were rejected by the normalizer for using them — measured against the corpus, not guessed. `review-by` stays even though no ADR carries it yet, because updateAdr emits it and #527 made it legal.
frontmatter._comment_newAdrStatus: A new decision is born `open` and stays `open` until someone records a resolution. This was hardcoded in writeAdr and nowhere else — true by accident rather than by decision. Declaring it here makes it a recorded rule, and `doc-maintenance.md` references this key. `open` is the only defensible birth state: a decision nobody has argued about yet has not been made.

_comment_case: normalizeStatus() folds case and strips brackets only. It does NOT map out-of-vocabulary values (CLOSED -> accepted): that is a one-time migration, deliberately not automatic, so a typo cannot be silently reinterpreted.
